newsitem.title: USA: Rodney King sentenced to work on roads.
newsitem.headline: Rodney King sentenced to work on roads.

text.p: Rodney King, whose videotaped beating by police ultimately led to the 1992 Los Angeles riots, was sentenced on Friday to serve 30 days on a road crew for violating probation on a drunk-driving charge.
Judge Bruce Marrs gave King, 31, until Jan. 13 to complete his service with the California state Department of Transportation.

The sentence stemmed from King's July 11 conviction for leaving the scene of an accident during an argument with his estranged wife. That conviction constituted a violation of a three-year probation King was placed on after a January, 1994 conviction of drunk driving.

Last month King was sentenced to 90 days in jail and two-years probation for the hit-and-run incident with his estranged wife, Crystal, although he was acquitted of spousal abuse, assault with a deadly weapon and reckless driving.
King made headlines in March 1991 when an amateur cameraman captured white Los Angeles police officers on videotape raining kicks and baton blows on him after a high speed car chase.

In April 1992 53 people died and more than 2,000 were injured and 9,500 arrested in rioting, looting and arson in Los Angeles after a jury in nearby Simi Valley acquitted four white officers in King's beating.
Two of the officers were later convicted on federal charges of violating King's civil rights.
